H_hierarchical.evidence: The top-level CONOPS is mostly a flat operational-mode FSM, but INIT is elaborated as an internal startup sequence beginning at a power-on pseudo-state, and the paper also describes a hierarchical FDIR architecture from unit to mission/system levels.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Mode switching depends on ground telecommand, task/init completion, battery below nominal, FDIR anomaly orders, sun visibility, battery <86%, battery >90%, and command validity checks.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: Mode behavior includes boot-counter update, delayed antenna deployment with retries, subsystem initialization, payload power-off, beacon-rate changes, receiver-on commandability, housekeeping persistence, image acquisition/compression/storage, downlink, logging, alarms, and resets.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: The paper defines hierarchical FDIR; for subsystem/system failures the safety monitor signals the flight planner to switch to SAFE, where non-vital units are powered off until ground contact.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: SAFE/CRITICAL/SUN-VIS/COMMUNICATION modes are described in CONOPS, while FDIR decision logic, safety-monitor signaling, logging, watchdogs, and safe-mode fallback details appear later in the application-layer implementation section.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Terms such as safe mode, fail-safe approach, hierarchical FDIR, safe-guarding configuration, and closed-mode CONOPS imply spacecraft fault-management rules beyond a simple event label.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: Actions are expressed in prose per mode rather than in a state table: payload off, beacon rate reduced, receiver always on, housekeeping persisted, ADCS low-power mode, command retries, alarms, and reset behavior.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: The flight planner executes delayed commands only during Sun-Vis mode when enough power is available; communication mode also combines attitude monitoring, battery checks, and threshold-triggered fallback.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: Although INIT has an internal startup sequence and the FDIR architecture is hierarchical, the paper does not clearly define a parent composite state with its own entry/during/exit behavior separate from child states.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: For failures at subsystem or system level, the safety monitor sends signals to the flight planner to switch to safe mode; SAFE is also entered after a system fault/failure event.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: INIT includes a power-on pseudo-state and a nontrivial startup chain with delayed antenna deployment, retry/reboot handling, subsystem initialization, and transition to SAFE, but no deep nested composite hierarchy is fully specified.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: There are several threshold and conjunction-style guards, including battery <86%, nominal/>90% battery, sun visibility, valid command checks, and Sun-Vis plus sufficient-power gating, but not enough explicit arithmetic/boolean guard formulas for strong SMT advantage.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: Global anomaly/failure handling routes subsystem/system failures to SAFE across the operational mode space, and periodic monitoring/checking behavior is described for communication, housekeeping, health, pings, and battery state.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: The controller uses abstract side effects such as event logging, error/failure reporting, alarms to higher FDIR levels, signals to the flight planner, telemetry counters, and ground reporting.

key_nl_quotes: Masat-1 operating modes are ruled by a finite state machine.
For failures at the subsystem or system level, the safety monitor sends signals to the flight planner to switch to safe mode.
one_line_pitch: This is a strong spacecraft-mode stress test because the modeler must recover mode guards, rich per-mode actions, and a global hierarchical FDIR safe-mode escape from prose spread across CONOPS and implementation sections.
rationale: The STM extraction is consistent with the paper's CONOPS and application-layer architecture: Masat-1 is explicitly governed by a finite-state operational-mode controller with battery, sun-visibility, task-completion, telecommand, and anomaly-triggered transitions. Its strongest stress-test value is in action attribution and global recovery: each mode has concrete operational side effects, while hierarchical FDIR routes major anomalies to SAFE. The hierarchy is not a fully nested statechart, but the INIT pseudo-state sequence and FDIR layers add enough structure to stress baselines beyond a flat event-only FSM.
